text: UTF-8 is described as self-synchronising. What does that buy?
choices: It can be decoded without knowing the byte order
Dropping into the middle of a stream, you can find the next character boundary by examining at most a few bytes
It automatically detects and corrects transmission errors
It guarantees that all characters occupy the same number of bytes
explanation: Continuation bytes always begin with the bits 10 and lead bytes never do, so a decoder that starts mid-stream can resynchronise within a few bytes. Compare Baudot's shift codes, where one corrupted shift character misinterprets everything after it — an unbounded corruption from a single lost bit.
